short: The lead ship of the US Navy's class of nuclear-powered supercarriers, symbolising American naval dominance.
full:
Commissioned on 3 May 1975, USS Nimitz (CVN-68) is the lead ship of her class of nuclear-powered aircraft carriers. Named after World War II Pacific fleet commander Chester W. Nimitz, it measures over a thousand feet in length and can carry up to ninety fixed-wing and rotary aircraft. Its early operational deployments included operations in the Indian Ocean during the Iran hostage crisis in 1980, including the aborted rescue mission Operation Eagle Claw.

The Nimitz class set the standard for modern supercarriers, defining American global force projection for over four decades. The sheer scale and capability of Nimitz and her nine sister ships have allowed the United States to maintain air superiority in conflicts ranging from the Gulf War to operations in Afghanistan and Iraq. As of the 2020s, Nimitz remains in active service as one of the oldest operational warships in the US Navy.
